title: Wednesday, September 9, 2026

headline.title: META closed +6.51% at 653.39 — and it closed above its own premarket mark, which is the first time a gap of this shape has done that in three weeks. It opened 645.35, ran to 657.86, and never traded below 642.34. The morning note called the Failed 2 Up voided over 624.80 and then attached the standing caution — that SNOW, GTLB, MRVL and ORCL all handed back a chunk of exactly this setup inside the session. That caution was wrong today, and the break in the pattern is worth more than the win.
headline.summary: Apple gave the whipsaw the event deserved and closed lower anyway. It opened 317.86 — precisely the level the note said had to be reclaimed — then fell to 312.95 in the first hour. During the 1:00pm keynote hour it printed a 319.15 high and a 309.90 low, a nine-point range on 10.8M shares, and closed 315.42, −0.25%, still under 317.86 for a fifth straight session. Underneath, breadth was ugly: nine of twelve sectors red, IWM −1.35% the worst index, and only XLE +0.83%, SMH +0.09% and XLK +0.03% green. The semi wall broke selectively — MRVL +4.25%, AMD +3.03%, MU +2.72% — while ASML −2.05% and TSM −0.81% went the other way.

what_happened: The gap-fade pattern broke, and that matters more than the trade.

Four times in three weeks this book documented the same shape: a large premarket gap into or out of a catalyst, and a regular session that handed a meaningful part of it back. SNOW, GTLB, MRVL, ORCL. This morning META gapped +5.8% to 648.99 and the note repeated the caution. Instead it opened 645.35, made its low in the first minutes at 642.34, and spent the entire session above the premarket print, closing 653.39 — +0.7% above where it was quoted before the bell. The pattern was four for four and is now four for five.
Apple's event produced a nine-point range and no resolution.

The 1:00pm CT keynote hour traded 309.90 to 319.15 on 10.8M shares, roughly three times any other hour of the session. It closed 315.42 — below where it opened, below the 317.86 level, and inside the range it made during the event itself. Five consecutive sessions now without reclaiming that level. After hours it is bid at 317.25, right back at the line, which means the actual answer to the pricing-power question has been deferred rather than given.
Breadth was the worst of the week.

Nine of twelve sectors red. Only XLE +0.83% had a real bid; SMH +0.09% and XLK +0.03% were flat, and everything else fell — XLI −1.50%, XLY −1.32%, XLP and XLU both −1.15%, XLRE −1.08%, XLB −1.06%. IWM −1.35% against SPY's −0.47% is nearly three times the damage, and it closed at 290.70, on its low. With Brent over $100 and the 10-year at 4.80% into tomorrow's PPI, the small-cap tape is where the rate pressure is showing first.

T1. Failed 2U reclaimed. Tuesday took Friday's 617.46 high to 624.80 and closed 613.48 under it. Over 624.80 voids the failure. The note's caution: “the last four gaps of this shape — SNOW, GTLB, MRVL, ORCL — all gave back a meaningful part of it inside the session. The opening range is the reference, not the print.”

The setup was right and the caution was wrong, which is the more useful half. It opened 645.35, put its low in immediately at 642.34, ran to 657.86, and closed 653.39 — above the 648.99 premarket quote. Anyone who waited for the opening-range pullback the note recommended got filled near 645 and did fine; anyone who waited for a deeper fade never got one. Four for five on the pattern now, and the exception was a mega cap with a $10.1M call ticket against a 60% bear lean.

Straightforward. It opened 148.50, already through the trigger, never traded below 147.755, and closed 149.94 against a 150.01 high — seven cents off the top. XOM +2.24% was the confirmation that mattered, with COP +1.16%, OXY +1.10% and XLE +0.83% behind it. The refiners lagged the crude move: VLO +1.58%, PSX +0.61%, MPC +0.39%.
STAYED BROKEN THROUGH ITS OWN EVENT

T1, flagged blue. 2 Down. Tuesday broke Friday's 317.86 low to 314.90 and closed under it. Under 317.86 it stays broken. The note said the event was midday, not at the open, and that a pricing-power question gets answered in the December quarter rather than on stage.

It opened 317.86 — exactly the level — and immediately failed, dropping to 312.95 within the hour. The keynote hour then ran 309.90 to 319.15 on 10.8M shares and it closed 315.42, still under. Directionally correct for a fifth straight session, but this was not a clean trade: the level was tagged at the open and again during the event, and anyone positioned through 1:00pm sat through a nine-point range for a quarter-percent result.

how_played_out: A documented pattern failed today, and that is the most valuable thing in this report.

Four separate sessions in three weeks produced the same result — SNOW, GTLB, MRVL, ORCL all gapped and all gave back a meaningful share of it inside the regular session — and this morning's note applied the rule to META and told readers to use the opening range rather than the print. META opened 645.35, made its low in the first minutes at 642.34, and closed 653.39, above the premarket quote. The rule is now four for five. What separates today is worth naming rather than smoothing over: META is a mega cap with a $10.1M single call ticket behind it against a 60% bear options lean, not a mid-cap reacting to its own print. Size and liquidity may be the variable the pattern was missing.
Apple gave the event range and refused to give the answer.

The keynote hour traded 309.90 to 319.15 — a 9.25-point range on 10.8M shares, about triple any other hour — and closed 315.42, inside that range and below the 317.86 level for a fifth straight session. Then after hours it bid to 317.25, back at the line. The morning note said a pricing-power question gets answered in the December quarter rather than on stage, and the tape agreed: maximum volatility, no resolution. The tradeable observation is that the level held as resistance through the single largest scheduled catalyst the name had this quarter.
The semi wall was a bucket, not a signal.

The morning read grouped SNDK, MU, IONQ, ASML, QCOM, KLAC, WDC and MRVL as a Failed 2U wall coiled under Tuesday's highs and said to wait for one of them to break. Half broke up and half broke down: MRVL +4.25%, AMD +3.03%, MU +2.72%, INTC +1.68%, SNDK +1.48% against ASML −2.05%, AVGO −1.12% and TSM −0.81%. SMH finished +0.09% — flat — because the two halves cancelled. Treating a shared Strat classification as a shared trade is the error; the bucket described the shape, not the direction.
Breadth deteriorated while the index barely moved.

SPY fell 0.47% and nine of twelve sectors closed red, with IWM −1.35% finishing on its low at 290.70. Only energy had a real bid. That combination — a quiet index, a broken small-cap tape, Brent over $100 and the 10-year at 4.80% — is the setup going into PPI tomorrow at 7:30am and CPI Friday. The index number is not describing what is happening underneath it, and it has not for four sessions.

darkpool.note: Tuesday's board was graded today and the index ask lean was right for a fourth straight session. IVV $1.5B ask was the largest print on the whole tape, with VOO $1.2B and SPY $1.0B behind it — and SPY closed −0.47%, its third consecutive lower close. The memory split resolved in favour of the one wearing the bid: MU carried $4.7B cumulative bid plus a $413M bid print after hours and closed +2.72%, while SNDK's $3.2B ask managed only +1.48% and NVDA's $5.1B mixed with a $750M ask closed −0.90%. That is three for three on the direction of the lean inside one sector. On the options side the loud tickets that disagreed with their own tape were vindicated twice: the $10.1M META call trade against a 60% bear lean closed +6.51%, and the $9.0M MRVL 270P block against a 60% bear lean went the wrong way as MRVL rose 4.25%. The badge was the crowd; the ticket was right on META and wrong on MRVL.

lessons: When a documented pattern fails, name the variable rather than the exception.

The gap-fade rule was four for four and is now four for five. The lazy move is to call META an outlier. The useful move is to note what is different: it is a mega cap with enormous liquidity, and the gap came from analyst repositioning rather than its own earnings print. Every one of the four that faded — SNOW, GTLB, MRVL, ORCL — was reacting to a scheduled company event. That is a testable distinction, and it should be tracked forward rather than settled today.
A shared Strat classification is not a shared trade.

Eight names sat in the Failed 2U bucket this morning and the note treated them as one wall. MRVL closed +4.25% and ASML closed −2.05%. SMH finished flat at +0.09% because the halves cancelled exactly. The bucket correctly described the shape — all coiled under Tuesday's highs — and said nothing about direction. Grouping them into a single line in the prep implied a correlation that did not exist.
The biggest scheduled catalyst can produce range without resolution.

Apple's keynote hour ran 309.90 to 319.15 on triple the session's average hourly volume, and the stock closed 315.42 — inside that range, below the level it needed, and then bid back to 317.25 after hours. Maximum volatility, zero information. Positioning ahead of an event on the assumption that the event decides something is the error; this one deferred the decision to the December quarter, exactly as the morning note said it would.
Watch IWM, not SPY, while oil is doing this.

SPY fell 0.47% and IWM fell 1.35%, closing on its low. Nine sectors red with only energy bid. With Brent through $100 and the 10-year at 4.80%, the rate pressure lands on the most leveraged, least liquid part of the tape first, and it has now done so for four consecutive sessions while the index looked calm. Into PPI tomorrow and CPI Friday, the small-cap print is the honest one.
tomorrow: August PPI at 7:30am CT with jobless claims, and the ECB statement at 7:15am with Lagarde at 7:45am. Three macro events inside forty-five minutes, and a 30-year auction at 12:00pm behind them with the 10-year at 4.80%. This is the heaviest morning of the week.

Reports post-close against a backlog of $638B, up 363% year-over-year. It closed 161.70, −0.50%, having already failed to hold a 5.5% gap once this week two days before the print. The question is whether that backlog converts to revenue.

Closed 653.39, forty points above Tuesday and above its own premarket, with nothing overhead. That cuts both ways — no resistance and no support. The 642.34 session low is the only reference it made today.

Closed 315.42, still under 317.86 for a fifth session, but bid 317.25 after hours. The level is the whole trade: reclaim it and the five-session downtrend is over; fail it again and the event resolved nothing in the bulls' favour.

Closed 290.70 on its low, −1.35%. It has now underperformed SPY on four straight sessions. If PPI runs hot tomorrow this is where it shows up first, and there is no near reference beneath today's low.

Carry into Thursday: the index has drifted 0.5% for three sessions while breadth rotted underneath and energy took the only real bid. Nothing has broken. But the setup into PPI and CPI is a narrow tape, Brent over $100, and a market pricing roughly 60% odds of a hike next week.
